title: Thousands demonstrate across Turkey against violence against women
seoTitle: Istanbul protest against violence on women

tea.why: Protesters gathered on the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women to oppose rising femicide and state policies.
tea.want: Demands included state action against femicide, the protection of women's rights, and a reversal of policies limiting gender equality.
tea.changed: Nov 25: Thousands demonstrated in multiple cities, including Istanbul, Ankara, and Diyarbakir, despite government bans on gatherings.

summary: On November 25, 2026, thousands of people participated in demonstrations across Turkey to mark the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women. In Istanbul, approximately 3,000 protesters gathered under heavy police presence after authorities prohibited marches at Taksim Square. Similar rallies occurred in Ankara, Diyarbakir, Izmir, and other locations. Organised by groups including the We Will Stop Femicide Platform, participants highlighted that 369 women have been killed in Turkey this year. Protesters criticised the government's 2021 withdrawal from the Istanbul Convention and argued that state policies fail to protect women from violence. While President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan addressed the issue by framing political and ideological pressure as violence, activists maintained that state-sanctioned male violence remains a systemic problem. Police maintained a blockade throughout the Istanbul event.
response: President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan stated that psychological pressure on women due to their political views, beliefs, or lifestyles constitutes violence. Authorities in Istanbul banned gatherings at Taksim Square and deployed heavy police presence to monitor the demonstrations.

updates.text: Thousands gathered in Istanbul, Ankara, Diyarbakir, and other cities to protest violence against women.
